results.name: Direct target with disease-gene association baseline
results.hypothesis: A chemical that directly physically interacts with a disease-associated gene may treat the disease.
results.mechanism_rationale: Direct molecular interaction is stronger than generic affects, but the rule lacks direction, functional consequence, and pathway corroboration.
results.trapi_notes: The two-edge path is directly expressible in TRAPI.

results.name: Affected disease gene with pathway corroboration
results.hypothesis: A chemical is more likely to treat a disease when it affects a disease-associated gene that participates in a process containing multiple additional genes associated with the same disease.
results.body: chemical -affects-> gene -gene_associated_with_condition-> disease; gene -involved_in-> process <-involved_in- corroborating genes -gene_associated_with_condition-> disease
results.mechanism_rationale: Requires a direct chemical target, disease association, and independent pathway-level disease-gene corroboration.
results.trapi_notes: The branched graph is expressible, but requiring at least two distinct corroborating genes needs post-processing or Cypher.
